wu: KET Speaking Speed Dating: Students stand in two lines facing each other. The teacher calls a topic (e.g., 'hobbies'), and students in one line ask 'What do you like doing in your free time?' to the person opposite. After 30 seconds, the teacher claps, and one line shifts to the right to speak to a new partner. Repeat 3 times.
wuAlt: KET Speaking Bingo: Students write 9 personal questions (e.g., 'Where do you live?') on a grid. They mingle, asking questions, and getting signatures from classmates who answer 'Yes'. First to get 3 in a row wins.

KET Speaking Relay: Teams race to write KET Part 1 questions on the board. Each student writes one question (e.g., 'How old are you?'), then passes the marker. First team with 10 correct questions wins.
pres: Show KET Speaking Part 1 flashcards (e.g., a house, a book, a football). Model answering 'Where do you live?' with 'I live in a house in Oujda.' Elicit similar answers for 'What do you read?' and 'What sports do you play?' Check understanding by asking students to repeat the model sentences chorally.
presAlt: Use a KET Speaking Part 1 dialogue script on the board. Read it aloud with a strong student, then have pairs read it in roles. Highlight the question-answer pattern.
Show a short video of two teens doing KET Speaking Part 1. Pause after each question, asking students to predict the answer. Discuss good responses.
prac: KET Speaking Part 1 Drill: Students work in pairs with a worksheet of 10 personal questions (e.g., 'What time do you get up?'). They take turns asking and answering, using the model language. Monitor and correct pronunciation. Give stickers for good eye contact.
pracAlt: KET Speaking Question Chain: Students sit in a circle. Student 1 asks a question to Student 2 (e.g., 'What's your favourite food?'). Student 2 answers then asks a new question to Student 3. Continue around the circle, with the teacher helping if a question repeats.
KET Speaking Flashcard Match: Students match question flashcards (e.g., 'How many siblings do you have?') to answer flashcards (e.g., 'I have two brothers.'). Then practice the pairs in groups.
ls: Play a KET Listening Part 1 audio where two teens introduce themselves. Students listen and tick the correct answers on a multiple-choice worksheet (e.g., 'What's Tom's favourite sport? A Football B Basketball'). Replay to check answers, focusing on names and details.
re: KET Speaking Two Corners: Label corners 'Agree' and 'Disagree'. Read a statement (e.g., 'Teenagers should have a mobile phone'). Students run to a corner and explain why using 'I agree because...' or 'I disagree because...'. Switch statements quickly to keep energy high.
prod: KET Speaking Part 2 Practice: Students work in pairs. Student A gets a card with a topic (e.g., 'My best friend') and must speak for 1 minute. Student B then asks 2 follow-up questions (e.g., 'How old is your friend?'). Swap roles. Time each turn and give feedback on fluency.
rw: KET Reading Part 4: Students read a short text about a Moroccan festival (e.g., Green March). They answer 5 multiple-choice questions by scanning for keywords. Then, write 2 sentences about their own favourite festival using 'I like...' and 'Because...'.
st: Play a KET Speaking-themed song (e.g., 'Hello, Hello, How Are You?'). End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we practiced KET Speaking Part 1-2. Great job, everyone! Thank you for your hard work. See you next week!'
g: Teams take turns answering KET Part 1 questions for points. If correct, they get 1 point; if they add a follow-up question, they get 2 points.
Students sit in a circle. Student 1 says 'My name is Ali and I like football'. Student 2 says 'My name is Sara and Ali likes football. I like reading'. Continue, adding names and hobbies.
Students draw cards with roles (e.g., 'new student', 'interviewer') and practice Part 1-2 conversations using prompts.
Students interview 3 different partners about their hobbies, family, and school. They write down 1 interesting fact from each interview.
Write 5 incorrect KET answers on the board (e.g., 'I like play football'). Students work in pairs to find and fix the errors.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a full KET Speaking Part 2 dialogue (questions and answers) about their dream holiday.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence starter worksheet (e.g., 'I live in...') to help with Part 1 answers.
hw: Write 5 quiz questions about KET Speaking Part 1 for next class (e.g., 'What's your favourite subject?').
Record yourself answering 3 KET Part 1 questions and bring it to class.
Draw a picture of your family and write 3 sentences about them using 'This is...' and 'He/She likes...'.
tip: For KET Speaking practice, focus on fluency over accuracy. Praise confident answers first, then gently correct errors. In the Moroccan context, encourage students to share local festivals or hobbies to build cultural pride.
